interest: Documents diplomatic and technical efforts to resolve Japanese radio jamming of American broadcasts and international frequency priority conflicts.
overview: This file documents coordinated efforts by the U.S. State Department, the Federal Communications Commission, and the Navy Department between 1939 and 1940 (alongside an isolated 1932 telegram) to address severe radio interference caused by Japanese broadcasting stations and maritime vessels. The records focus heavily on Japanese stations JZI, JZJ, JDK, JND, and Shanghai's XJOB jamming or disrupting American transmissions—particularly shortwave broadcasts from station KGEI (formerly W6XBE) in San Francisco, Press Wireless circuits to Manila, and naval communications. The documentation details civilian and diplomatic listener complaints, technical monitoring of frequency deviations and harmonic emissions, U.S. priority claims under international radio agreements, and formal diplomatic protests lodged with the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
